mcqs.learning_point: Understand its role in local decision-making
mcqs.question: Which statement best defines the Gram Sabha and distinguishes its role in local decision‑making from that of the Gram Panchayat?

options.A: The Gram Sabha is the gathering of all adult villagers that directly decides on development plans, while the Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body that implements those decisions.
options.B: The Gram Sabha is the elected council that executes policies, whereas the Gram Panchayat is a forum for all villagers to discuss issues.
options.C: The Gram Sabha is a state‑level legislative assembly, and the Gram Panchayat is a local judicial body.
options.D: The Gram Sabha functions as a court for village disputes, while the Gram Panchayat handles financial matters.

mcqs.answer: The Gram Sabha is the gathering of all adult villagers that directly decides on development plans, while the Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body that implements those decisions.
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly states that the Gram Sabha comprises all adult residents and makes decisions on development, whereas the Gram Panchayat is the elected body that carries out those decisions. Options B, C and D misrepresent the composition and functions of the two institutions.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the importance of discussion and participation
mcqs.question: During a Gram Sabha meeting, villagers discuss the construction of a new well. Why is this discussion important for the project’s success?

options.A: It allows the village leader to announce the project without opposition.
options.B: It ensures that the needs and suggestions of the community are heard, leading to broader acceptance and better planning.
options.C: It delays the project so that external agencies can take over.
options.D: It replaces the need for any technical expertise in the project.

mcqs.answer: It ensures that the needs and suggestions of the community are heard, leading to broader acceptance and better planning.
mcqs.explanation: Option B highlights that discussion lets villagers voice their needs, which improves planning and acceptance. Option A ignores participation, C incorrectly suggests delay is beneficial, and D wrongly assumes discussion substitutes technical input.

mcqs.question: A Gram Sabha learns that the Gram Panchayat has spent money meant for road repair on unrelated items. Which action best illustrates the Gram Sabha exercising local accountability?

options.A: The Gram Sabha files a complaint with the state government without discussing it locally.
options.B: The Gram Sabha questions the Panchayat’s expenditure, demands a public audit, and decides on corrective measures.
options.C: The Gram Sabha ignores the issue and proceeds with the next meeting.
options.D: The Gram Sabha appoints a new Sarpanch without investigating the spending.

mcqs.answer: The Gram Sabha questions the Panchayat’s expenditure, demands a public audit, and decides on corrective measures.
mcqs.explanation: Option B shows the Gram Sabha directly holding the Panchayat accountable by seeking transparency and corrective action. Options A, C, and D either bypass local mechanisms or ignore accountability.

mcqs.question: In Village X, the Gram Sabha meets every month, and all adult residents vote on the allocation of funds for a school library. Which of the following best describes the Gram Sabha’s function in this scenario?

options.A: A judicial body that settles disputes over library books.
options.B: A forum where only elected officials decide on fund allocation.
options.C: A platform that enables every villager to participate directly in deciding how public resources are used.
options.D: A committee that prepares the state’s education policy.

mcqs.answer: A platform that enables every villager to participate directly in deciding how public resources are used.
mcqs.explanation: Option C correctly captures that the Gram Sabha allows all villagers to take part in decisions about public funds. Options A, B, and D mischaracterize its role.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise who participates in the Gram Sabha
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about participation in a Gram Sabha is correct?

options.A: Only the Sarpanch and the members of the Gram Panchayat are allowed to attend.
options.B: All adult residents of the village, regardless of gender or caste, have the right to attend and speak.
options.C: Only men above the age of 21 may participate in the Gram Sabha.
options.D: Participation is limited to households that own land in the village.

mcqs.answer: All adult residents of the village, regardless of gender or caste, have the right to attend and speak.
mcqs.explanation: Option B reflects the constitutional provision that every adult villager can participate in the Gram Sabha. Options A, C, and D incorrectly restrict participation.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand its role in local decision-making
mcqs.question: Why does the involvement of the Gram Sabha in deciding village projects generally lead to better outcomes?

options.A: Because decisions are made by a single leader, ensuring speed.
options.B: Because the Gram Sabha’s collective input reflects the diverse needs of the community, increasing relevance and acceptance of decisions.
options.C: Because it eliminates the need for any technical expertise in project planning.
options.D: Because it allows the state government to directly control village resources.

mcqs.answer: Because the Gram Sabha’s collective input reflects the diverse needs of the community, increasing relevance and acceptance of decisions.
mcqs.explanation: Option B explains that broad participation captures varied community needs, leading to more appropriate and accepted decisions. Options A, C, and D misrepresent the benefits of Gram Sabha involvement.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the importance of discussion and participation
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares a Gram Sabha meeting with a Gram Panchayat meeting?

options.A: Both meetings include only elected representatives, so there is no difference in participation.
options.B: A Gram Sabha includes all adult villagers, fostering wider discussion, whereas a Gram Panchayat meeting involves only the elected members of the Panchayat.
options.C: A Gram Panchayat meeting is held annually, while a Gram Sabha meets daily.
options.D: The Gram Sabha decides on national policies, while the Gram Panchayat focuses on local issues.

mcqs.answer: A Gram Sabha includes all adult villagers, fostering wider discussion, whereas a Gram Panchayat meeting involves only the elected members of the Panchayat.
mcqs.explanation: Option B accurately contrasts the inclusive nature of the Gram Sabha with the more limited membership of Gram Panchayat meetings. Options A, C, and D are factually incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Gram Sabha in ensuring accountability of the Gram Panchayat?

options.A: Reviewing and approving the Panchayat’s annual development plan.
options.B: Auditing the Panchayat’s expenditure of funds allocated for village projects.
options.C: Appointing teachers to the village primary school.
options.D: Discussing grievances of villagers and directing corrective action.

mcqs.answer: Appointing teachers to the village primary school.
mcqs.explanation: Option C is not a function of the Gram Sabha; teacher appointments are handled by the education department. Options A, B, and D are legitimate accountability functions of the Gram Sabha.
